newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New Zealander emerges as Burns Philp buyer.
newsitem.headline: New Zealander emerges as Burns Philp buyer.

text.p: New Zealand entrepreneur Graeme Hart emerged on Monday as the mystery buyer of a 16.24 percent stake in ailing Australian food group Burns, Philp & Co Ltd.
Hart had been suggested as a possible buyer after selling his Whitcoulls printing and book retailing group last year for NZ$320 million (US$221 million).
Hart met Burns Philp management before announcing his interest, and said later he intended to remain a long-term shareholder.
He also said in a statement he "identified" with Burns Philp's current objectives.

However, analysts suggested his interest would give him leverage in the event of a takeover bid for the company, which has abandoned its strategy of becoming a major player in the herbs and spice market, and is seeking a new chief executive.
"I think it's very much an opportunistic move," said a Sydney-based analyst. "But he's got to wait for someone to come in, which is a very big gamble."
A Burns Philp spokesman said board representation was also briefly discussed, but it was agreed it was not an immediate priority for either Hart or Burns Philp.

Burns Philp has been seen as a potential takeover target following its exit from herbs and spices, with fellow Australian food group Goodman Fielder Ltd keen to acquire its well performed yeast business.

However, the group's future has been clouded by on-going litigation over the A$600 million (US$450 million) collapse of Estate Mortgage Trusts in 1990. A Burns Philp subsidiary was the Estate Mortgage trustee.
Analysts said Hart may have taken a view about the litigation in his decision to build up a strategic stake.
However, he appeared to have little to offer Burns Philp, while another food company may have been able to extract savings through synergies, they said.
Analysts also said the New Zealander, who spent A$2.50 a share to acquire the bulk of his stake, an investment of about A$210 million, also appeared to have paid over the odds.
Burns Philp closed at A$2.03 last Thursday before news of the share raid and had traded in the A$2.00 to A$2.20 range in recent months.
"If he'd just sat in the market he could have picked it up for 25 cents a share less," said one analyst.
Burns Philp closed down 3.8 cents at A$2.392 on Monday, a level which values Hart's shareholding at A$206 million.
